newsitem.title: USA: Calpine sets Texas power plant.
newsitem.headline: Calpine sets Texas power plant.

text.p: Calpine Corp said Friday it has agreed with Phillips Petroleum Co to develop a 240-megawatt natural gas-fired merchant power facility in Pasadena, Texas.
A merchant facility is intended to serve a mix of customers in a market area without being fully committed to long-term power sales agreements, Calpine explained.

The company said it will own and operate the facility, providing 90 megawatts of electricity and 200,000 pounds per hour of steam to the Phillips Houston Chemical Complex under a firm and fixed-price long-term contract.
Calling the plant Pasadena I, Calpine said it is the first U.S. merchant facility to be developed and funded with non-recourse debt by an independent power company.
Claiming the plant "will be the lowest cost power producer selling into the Texas open market," Calpine said it will market the remaining electricity to that market.
The company said Pasadena 1 is the first of a series of merchant plants it will develop in the United States.
In addition to owning and operating the facility, the company will apply its fully integrated approach to developing power projects -- Calpine-Construct.
Calpine said it will manage the engineering, arrange non-recourse financing, procure the major equipment and fuel, and manage the construction of the facility.

As announced earlier this year, the permitting process is under way. ING Capital Corp has committed to provide about $150 million of non-recourse project financing. Calpine expects to complete financing and begin construction in the fourth quarter, with commercial operation scheduled to begin in August 1998, it said.
